correctness.rationale: Actual seven-file Git source package at frozen commit was read, and its seven blob IDs reconstructed to exact assigned tree SHA. For each integer q>=3, real gamma>0 and nonconstant finite Blaschke B, input vectors e_k=(k+1)^(gamma/2) z^(q^k), k>=1, have norm one. For nonmonomial B, its real-analytic boundary phase is nonaffine; compact finite cover by intervals where some phase derivative of order >=2 stays nonzero gives a uniform-in-frequency oscillatory-integral bound C N^(-eta), eta>0. Any origin-zero factors only shift Fourier frequencies. Since B is rational analytic across the unit circle, choose R>1 and A>log(M_R)/log R: Cauchy bounds the m>AN squared tail exponentially; <=1+log_q(AN) exceptional frequencies remain below, so their total squared coefficient mass is o(1). Parseval for inner B gives ||B^N||_beta^2=1-o(1). Taking N=q^k proves the exact normalized-output coefficient one and excludes bounded extension. Monomial B=xi z^d acts by mutually orthogonal columns with squared ratio beta_{dn}/beta_n: q-power degrees have norm exactly one (attained on constants), infinitely many unaffected columns force noncompactness; every other d gives ratio (k+1)^gamma for n=q^k. HS equality is a separate fully attributed consequence of Cruz-Zamorano et al. Theorem 1.3(b), q>2 and inf q^k/(k+1)^gamma>0. Independent checker performed 14,448 allowed monomial ratios, 1,230 forbidden exact ratios, and 30 nonmonomial finite FFT experiments including 0,1,2 zeros at zero, not a proof for all powers. No logical gap found.

evidence: BFZ 2024 Theorem 1 (also DOI:10.1093/imrn/rnae199): stronger coefficientwise decay uniform over m for nonmonomial finite Blaschke powers, independent of any weighted Hardy choice.
Cruz-Zamorano–Dellepiane–Seco 2026 Theorem 1.3(b): for q>2 and exceptional indices Lambda, equality HS(beta)=HS(1) iff inf N_k beta_{N_k}>0; holds because q^k/(k+1)^gamma has positive infimum.

Lefèvre et al. Theorem 1.2 addresses every composition symbol and Theorem 4.9 necessary slow oscillation for nontrivial disk automorphism; the constructed sparse weight fails slow oscillation and global all-symbol hypotheses.

Hou–Jiang Definition 1.1 requires w_k=beta_k/beta_{k-1} to converge to one (after reconciling their squared-weight normalization); the sharp sparse dips violate this, so their Fredholm/closed-range theorems do not dominate this case.

evidence: Let A_N(m)=widehat(B^N)(m). BFZ gives sup_m |A_N(m)|<=C N^{-eta} for each fixed nonmonomial finite Blaschke B; adding any z^r factor shifts the spectrum and does not change the supremum.
Analytic extension to |z|<=R>1 gives |A_N(m)|<=M_R^N R^{-m}. For A>log(M_R)/log R, the squared tail m>AN is exponentially small.

There are <=1+log_q(AN) exceptional indices q^j<=AN, giving exceptional Fourier mass <=C^2(1+log_q AN)N^{-2eta}+O(e^{-cN})=o(1). Parseval gives ||B^N||_{H2(beta)}^2=1-o(1). With N=q^k, divide by beta_{q^k}=(k+1)^(-gamma) to obtain the claimed universal coefficient 1 and unboundedness.

For B=xi z^d, squared normalized column ratio is beta_{dn}/beta_n. If d=q^j this is <=1 with equality on constants, and infinite unaffected columns imply noncompactness; otherwise n=q^k gives ratio (k+1)^gamma exactly. Thus the entire classification is a short direct corollary of the cited BFZ estimate and elementary weight facts.

originality.rationale: The correct primary finding is a direct analytic corollary of established strong Fourier coefficient decay for finite Blaschke powers (BFZ 2024 Theorem 1) and elementary Cauchy-tail/Parseval and monomial weight-ratio observations. The general earlier theorem already implies that no Fourier mass remains on logarithmically sparse indices, hence the exact claimed growth coefficient one. The Hilbert–Schmidt equality is explicitly prior (Cruz-Zamorano et al. Theorem 1.3(b)); the degree-one nonrotation obstruction is also covered by Lefèvre et al. Theorem 4.9. No paper prints the same full semigroup statement word-for-word, but under implication-based originality this presentation does not yield an independently unknown result.
residual_risks: The cited BFZ Theorem 1 uses a convention avoiding zeros at the origin; the present extension is justified by shifting Fourier indices, not by claiming the theorem verbatim covers that convention.

The full finite-inner classification is not printed verbatim in any of the inspected prior papers, but follows immediately by mathematical implication; scientific priority is judged at the level of the claim, not title.
